To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Appalachian college campus is an isolated, insular, and socially irresponsible institution that is not preparing its students to meet the problems and challenges they will face in their home communities.

(1) the majority of Appalachian students are dissatisfied with the university experience and with their college education; (2) the dissatisfaction of Appalachian students is a result of the fact that the university is not a place of higher learning for the majority of Appalachian college students, and (3) the university is not an effective place of higher learning because it is structured to breed insularity and social responsibility, not enlightenment.
(1) The students who are most likely to drop out of Appalachian universities are the ones who have the most to gain by staying in school.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between the Appalachian college student and his university, and with the role of the university as a socializing institution.
the relationship of higher education to the economic development of the Appalachian region.

the ways in which the social and cultural characteristics of Appalachian communities influence the attitudes and behavior of their residents, and how these attitudes and behaviors affect their participation in higher education.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Appalachian universities are not the best institutions to serve the educational and social needs of the Appalachian people.
the Appalachian college student is in the same boat as his or her counterpart in other parts of the country.
the present system of higher education in Appalachia does not adequately meet the needs and interests of the region.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the students are not the only ones who have to be able to understand the students.
the Appalachian college student has not been adequately prepared for the demands of college life.
we have found that the college student's dissatisfaction with the university is a symptom of a more basic dissatisfaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to be careful about how we frame and present our work to students and to communities.

we need to be thinking more about how we can help students develop the skills and mindsets they will need to thrive in a world where the nature of work is rapidly changing, and to do so in a manner that is equitable and inclusive.
the Appalachian region is not a homogeneous place, and it is important to understand the diversity within it.
